statement: For binary classification with true class label $y \in \{0, 1\}$ and predicted probability $q_{y=1} = \hat{y} \equiv g(\mathbf{w} \cdot \mathbf{x}) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-\mathbf{w} \cdot \mathbf{x}}}$, the cross-entropy loss (also known as log loss, logarithmic loss, or logistic loss) between the true label distribution $p \in \{y, 1-y\}$ and the model predicted distribution $q \in \{\hat{y}, 1-\hat{y}\}$ is defined as $H(p, q) = -\sum_m p_m \log q_m = -y \log \hat{y} - (1-y) \log(1-\hat{y})$. For a dataset of $N$ observations, the average loss is $J(\mathbf{w}) = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N H(p_i, q_i) = -\frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N [y_i \log \hat{y}_i + (1-y_i) \log(1-\hat{y}_i)]$, and the total unnormalized loss is $L(\mathbf{w}) = -\sum_{i=1}^N [y_i \ln \hat{y}_i + (1-y_i) \ln(1-\hat{y}_i)]$.

properties.property: Gradient of cross-entropy loss with respect to weights equals the gradient of linear regression squared error
properties.why: Differentiating $L(\mathbf{w})$ with respect to weights $\mathbf{w}$ produces $\nabla_{\mathbf{w}} L(\mathbf{w}) = X^{\mathsf{T}}(\hat{\mathbf{y}} - \mathbf{y})$

properties.property: Cross-entropy minimization is equivalent to maximum likelihood estimation
properties.why: The log-likelihood satisfies $\log \mathcal{L}(\theta; \mathbf{x}) = -N \cdot H(p, q_\theta)$, so maximizing log-likelihood minimizes cross-entropy

properties.property: Cross-entropy attains its minimum value when the model distribution matches the true distribution
properties.why: By Gibbs' inequality, $H(p, q)$ reaches its minimum value $\mathrm{H}(p)$ when $p = q$, being identical to KL divergence up to an additive constant when reference distribution $p$ is fixed

properties.property: Log loss and cross-entropy loss are interchangeable terms in machine learning
properties.why: Cross-entropy between true label $p_i$ and model prediction $q_i$ is also defined as log loss, logarithmic loss, or logistic loss

assumptions.assumption: The true reference distribution p is fixed while the model distribution q is optimized
assumptions.breaks_when: Distribution q is the fixed prior reference and p is optimized under constraints, in which case cross-entropy minimization and KL divergence minimization are no longer equivalent

assumptions.assumption: Predicted probabilities \hat{y} lie strictly in the open interval (0, 1)
assumptions.breaks_when: A prediction reaches 0 or 1 such that \log(\hat{y}) or \log(1 - \hat{y}) evaluates \log(0)

failure_modes.signature: Loss evaluates to infinity or NaN
failure_modes.cause: Predicted probability $\hat{y}_i = 0$ when true label $y_i = 1$, or $\hat{y}_i = 1$ when $y_i = 0$, causing computation of $\log(0)$

failure_modes.mode: Inconsistent minimization under prior reference optimization
failure_modes.signature: Optimization yields solutions that do not correspond to KL divergence minimization
failure_modes.cause: Optimizing $p$ relative to a fixed prior distribution $q$, where cross-entropy $H(p, q)$ and relative entropy $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p \parallel q)$ diverge by more than an additive constant
